/-!
# Erdős Problem 406

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/406](https://www.erdosproblems.com/406)
-/

namespace Erdos406

/--
Is it true that there are only finitely many powers of $2$ which have only the digits $0$
and $1$ when written in base $3$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_406 : answer(sorry) ↔ { n | n.isPowerOfTwo ∧ Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [0, 1] }.Finite := by
  sorry

/--
If we only allow the digits $1$ and $2$ then $2^{15}$ seems to be the largest such power
of $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_406.variants.one_two :
    IsGreatest { n | n.isPowerOfTwo ∧ Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [1, 2] } (2 ^ 15) := by
  sorry

end Erdos406

reformulations.difference: Compared with Lagarias's finiteness formulation, Lean counts the numerical powers rather than their exponents and expresses omission of digit 2 using the list-subset condition Nat.digits 3 n ⊆ [0, 1].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ternary digit is less than 3, so this subset condition is equivalent to absence of digit 2. Nat.isPowerOfTwo n means ∃ k : ℕ, n = 2^k. The map k ↦ 2^k is injective, and the Lean set is exactly the image of the exceptional-exponent set under this map; hence their finiteness is equivalent. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: OEIS A104320 states that every exponent k > 15 produces a zero ternary digit; Lean instead asserts that 2^15 is the greatest power using only digits 1 and 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The allowed-digit condition is equivalent to absence of zero. Direct computation establishes that 2^15 satisfies it, and strict monotonicity of k ↦ 2^k makes the upper bound 2^k ≤ 2^15 equivalent to k ≤ 15. Thus IsGreatest is equivalent to ∀ k > 15, 0 ∈ Nat.digits 3 (2^k). This biconditional was proved in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: J. C. Lagarias, Ternary Expansions of Powers of 2, abstract and Introduction, explicitly distinguishing the finiteness conjecture from the stronger three-exception conjecture: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0512006
R. I. Saye, On two conjectures concerning the ternary digits of powers of two, abstract, Introduction, and computational conclusions: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2202.13256
T. Stérin and D. Woods, Hardness of busy beaver value BB(15), conjecture statement and number-theoretic background: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2107.12475
OEIS A104320, official sequence data, including Sloane's conjecture that a(n) > 0 for n > 15: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A104/A104320.seq

OEIS A102483, official sequence data, including the exceptional exponents 0,1,2,3,4,15 and the statement that completeness remains open: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A102/A102483.seq

review.notes: Both declarations were inspected and tested. Nat.isPowerOfTwo excludes zero, so Nat.digits 3 0 = [] causes no degeneracy. List subset ignores multiplicity and correctly allows repeated digits. Tests for exponents below 200 gave [0,2,8] and [0,1,2,3,4,15], respectively. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings; its equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Available community metadata and OEIS agree with open status. The cited webpage could not be read despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the independent mathematical sources above support both formulations.
